sheets.name: Outside_A1.png
sheets.prompt: Use case: style-transfer. Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET, a technical RPG Maker MZ tilesheet. Images 2 and 3 are STYLE REFERENCES. Completely REDRAW the materials with the reference maps' delicate handmade ink-on-parchment illustration. This is NOT a recolor: remove photorealistic/pixel shaded volumes, bevels, glossy highlights and noisy tiny texture. Use broad flat pale golden paper fills, fine slightly irregular dark brown outlines, small irregular polygon stones, sparse ink stippling, subtle hatching concentrated at cast shadows and crevices. The palette is pale parchment with fine dark ink, not a brown midtone wash. Preserve all subjects, atlas arrangement, all coordinates relative to the sheet, scale, footprints, transitions and transparent holes. Keep the exact aspect ratio of image 1, fill the entire canvas without margins. Technical geometry: native tiles 48x48, autotile quarters 24x24; keep all tile pieces on their original grid. Material transitions, opposite edges and matching quarter pieces must continue seamlessly when assembled. Do not invent text, gridlines, margins, objects, or paper outside the opaque areas. Blank areas remain real transparency. White stone, snow and other white source objects are OPAQUE and must become pale cream, never transparent. Retain all items even where science-fiction. Water animation atlas 4:3. Keep all animation frames with subtle differences in ripple positions. Redraw water as mostly light empty paper with fine horizontal ink ripples, banks as thin irregular outlines with sparse dots. Water must remain opaque. Keep reeds and plants in their places. Do not rearrange the three repeated frames.

sheets.name: Outside_A2.png
sheets.prompt: Edit target image 1: RPG Maker MZ terrain autotile atlas Outside_A2, native aspect ratio 4:3, 768x576. Images 2 and 3 are the exact desired illustration style. REDRAW image 1 as flat hand-drawn cartography in fine brown ink on pale golden parchment. This is NOT a sepia color filter: simplify noisy grass into almost empty parchment with sparse tiny speckles, replace shiny stone with clean flat irregular polygon stones and thin pen outlines, simplify hedge leaves to soft light shapes with narrow stippled shadows, eliminate 3D highlights and bevel shading. Use very fine contour lines, warm cream material fills, sparse hand-placed dots, almost no midtone wash. The art must feel like the two reference maps, not vintage tinted pixel art. Keep every terrain tile patch, transition shape, hole, fence, floor decoration and cell exactly in its current location. Keep its footprint and precise alignment; no rearrangement, no new objects, no margins. It is a technical tile atlas, not a composed map. Each source autotile block is 96x144 pixels, assembled from 24 pixel quarters: opposite edges and repeated transition quadrants must join seamlessly. Match native aspect ratio, preserve ALL transparent gaps and holes with real alpha. No overall paper background behind transparent regions. Keep filled terrain areas opaque pale golden parchment. Fine minimal lines, thin irregular polygon stones, subtle speckled soil; stronger ink only at boundaries and crevices. No text, no drawn grid.
